newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac consortium wins Cairo tunnel work.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac consortium wins Cairo tunnel work.

text.p: UK construction group Tarmac Plc said on Friday that an Anglo-Egyptian consortium, of which it is a part, has been awarded a 50 million stg contract to construct more than eight kilometres of tunnels beneath Cairo as part of a scheme to expand and improve the city's sewerage system.
The contract is the latest phase of one of the world's biggest and most difficult tunnelling projects, the company said in a statement.
The consortium is headed by Tarmac in joint venture with UK partners Balfour Beatty, Edmund Nuttall and Trafalgar House, together with Egyptian company The Arab Contractors.
Initially, the contract will run in parallel with another similar 90 million stg contract previously awarded to the consortium and due to finish in about a year.
This phase brings to nearly 400 million stg the total value of work carried out on the Cairo project by the consortium since 1985.
